articles.title: Keeping local radio information available when internet access fails
articles.summary: A saved station list helps find broadcasts without assuming that they are current or always available.

visual.alt: A checklist of planning prompts: Station, Frequency, Check date. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Record local radio stations that you have tuned or checked against broadcaster information, including their service name and the region served. Frequencies and local output can vary by transmitter.
A streaming phone app still needs connectivity, unlike a suitable broadcast receiver. Note whether your household device supports FM, AM or DAB and where its operating instructions are kept.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Write a clear paper station list and the date you last checked it. Include compatible battery details where relevant, without promising a listening duration.
Broadcast reception can fail and programmes may not concern your area. A saved station list is a way to seek information, not evidence of a current official warning.

articles.title: Preparing for a temporary ferry terminal or boarding-point change
articles.summary: Ferry operators can change boarding arrangements without cancelling the whole service.

visual.alt: A route of planning prompts: Booked terminal, Operator notice, Access check. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Keep the booked operator, sailing reference and named terminal available. Similar pier names do not establish that passengers may board at an adjacent berth.
Separate changes to boarding points from cancellation notices. Foot passengers, cyclists and vehicle passengers may receive different instructions.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Before departure, confirm current operator instructions and accessible access, including any longer walk or different interchange. Ask the operator when arrangements are unclear.
Follow terminal staff and restricted-area signs. A saved offline diagram cannot verify sailing status or grant access to a berth.

articles.title: Planning around a temporarily unavailable car-sharing bay
articles.summary: A shared vehicle may be booked while its usual parking bay is closed or relocated.

visual.alt: A sequence of planning prompts: Check booking, Confirm bay, Plan fallback. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Keep the car-share provider's official support channel and booking reference in a private place. A closed bay and a cancelled reservation are different problems.
Do not assume a shared vehicle may be collected or returned in any nearby parking space. Provider rules and local parking restrictions still apply.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Check the provider's latest authorised collection and return instructions before setting out. Consider another transport option when a fixed arrival time matters.
If a bay is blocked, ask the provider for an approved alternative and save the case reference. Never leave a vehicle in a restricted location based on an old map.

articles.title: Keeping parcel collection details when a shared locker is unavailable
articles.summary: A communal or public parcel locker fault may delay collection without losing the delivery record.

visual.alt: A checklist of planning prompts: Carrier, Collection code, Support. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Identify the carrier or locker operator on the original notification. Store parcel references and collection deadlines privately, not on a communal noticeboard.
An inaccessible locker does not mean the parcel is lost. Redirected collection, code validity and deadlines depend on the operator.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Use the carrier's current official channel to establish whether the parcel is held or redirected. Do not force a locker compartment or use someone else's code.
Record any support reference and confirm the authorised collection point before travelling. Remove expired access codes from shared devices.

articles.title: Making an offline roadside assistance contact card
articles.summary: A compact contact card can help a driver locate breakdown support information without mobile data.

visual.alt: A shelves of planning prompts: Provider, Policy reference, Vehicle details. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Write down the breakdown provider, membership reference and official contact details. Keep account passwords and sensitive information off a visible dashboard card.
Check the actual policy coverage for the vehicle and driver. A number copied from an old leaflet may no longer be correct.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Keep basic vehicle identification available to the authorised driver and agree who will contact support if travelling together.
This is an administrative record, not a vehicle-repair or roadside-positioning procedure. Follow current emergency and road-authority instructions in dangerous locations.

articles.title: Recording a damaged public wayfinding sign for reporting
articles.summary: Missing or obscured signs can make public routes difficult to follow, especially for visitors.

visual.alt: A checklist of planning prompts: Sign location, Problem, Report route. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: From a normal public position, note the street or facility, the sign's intended direction and what is unreadable or missing. Never enter restricted roadworks to inspect it.
Distinguish official wayfinding from advertising or event signs because different organisations may maintain them.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Report the fault through the relevant council, transport operator or site manager and retain a case reference. Photograph only when safe and respectful of bystanders.
Use other authorised signs or current operator information rather than guessing through a closed passage. This offline note is not a verified route map.

articles.title: Preparing a pet-care handover when travel is unexpectedly delayed
articles.summary: An agreed backup carer can make routine pet arrangements clearer during delayed journeys.

visual.alt: A sequence of planning prompts: Agree helper, Share routine, Confirm handover. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Ask a trusted person beforehand whether they can help with routine pet care. Do not assume a neighbour has agreed to enter the home.
Keep a private note of the animal's routine, usual supplies and veterinary contact. Do not post access codes or keys in a public message.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Agree how the helper will confirm that care has been provided and identify another authorised contact if the first person is unavailable.
Animals with medical or behavioural needs may require professional instructions. This article does not prescribe feeding amounts, treatment or unfamiliar-animal handling.

articles.title: Checking whether a public bicycle repair point is available
articles.summary: A public bicycle pump or repair stand may be unavailable during an ordinary journey.

visual.alt: A checklist of planning prompts: Locate facility, Check condition, Backup option. This is not live service information or an authorised route.
visual.caption: Offline reference; verify current details with the responsible operator.

sections.title: Understand the situation
paragraphs: Record the location and responsible operator of a public bicycle repair stand on a regular route. A map marker does not confirm its equipment works.
From a normal public position, look for a closure notice or obvious damage. Avoid using broken equipment or obstructing pedestrians.

sections.title: Prepare and follow up
paragraphs: Plan an alternative such as a staffed cycle shop or another transport option when a journey depends on a working bicycle. Confirm business hours when relevant.
Report damaged public equipment through the responsible scheme's official channel. This planning guide does not provide mechanical repair procedures.
